I am stupid. I love the simulacra series I really do, I saw it had bad reviews and I though eh they are normally reviewed pretty badly but it scratched an itch that no other games do. But what the f*** was that. That was not a simulacra game. That was a mess of cheap horror. [spoiler] Like wtf was the 3D model of the Beldam, why was she shiny!?! The death scenes of characters, seeing the goofy ah face of the Beldam. It looked awful.  And why did I become the security guard from while looking at Pauls house?! Like springtrap luring s***[/spoiler]

I didnt feel any tension at all during the game , nor did I care about the characters. Like they could die and I would feel fine. [spoiler] I suppose they could of and Paul did, but I'm such an epic gamer and saved everyone in an 'tense' battle against the simulacra, by giving Ruby moral support. I didnt even get to talk to the simulacra :(. I guess I learnt if my friends get possessed I will tell them to have a cup of tea and have a hot bath. [/spoiler]

The game also never  caught my attention, half the time I just got my 3DS out and started playing my silly little fashion game while I listen to those damn tapes. It was boring. 

I honestly have wasted my money. I have learnt my lesson I suppose. I will now sulk about this for a few weeks while I reminisce about the money that used to be in my bank.

review_text_raw: In the context of the rest of the series, this game feels lazy and rushed. The scenes featuring choices have horrible CG—while the previous games in the series didn't have great CG, it was at least passable; here, it's downright terrible. There are also awkward, jarring cuts after selecting choices during some character dialogue scenes. The ending is particularly disappointing, as it simply dumps exposition in text rather than showcasing the events through actual filmed or designed sequences like the first two games did. Overall, I’d recommend skipping this one. While the story itself isn’t bad, the execution is lacking in almost every way.

review_text_raw: This game is disappointing. At least the first two games allow the chat prompt to be instant and some extent, skip FMW/cutscenes (well Simulacra 1 did). This one does not even give you the option to speed up the game after completing it. Even the cutscene/FMV were too long, winded and boring. A truly let down game and I refuse to play it again to get all the achievements. It is a huge downgrade from the first two. Either implement skippable option and instant chat function, otherwise, this game is just going to be daunting for people to play.

review_text_raw:
Even with only 3 hours this game feels like it drags on forever. New characters are introduced way late into the game so you don't give a crap about them, and the ones they do use are just one dimensional exposition dumps with nothing interesting behind them. Unlocking new information on the phone wasn't rewarding, and some of the puzzles were way too tedious, looking for a single spec of information in a sea of nothing. I played this with a group and we were all angry when we figured out a puzzle, they just don't work.

Worst part is, this fails as a horror game as well. The scawy ghost is shown to you constantly so there's no fear of the unknown. The repetition of the symbol isn't scary, it's just goofy. The best part of the game is when the background freaked out and that was the only thing with any interest. It lasts a whole 15 seconds. Every video is just a nothing burger with the person 'seeing something in the distance.' Think paranormal activity 2 levels of boring surveillance. 

It fails at horror, fails at a compelling story, no interesting character, and no fun puzzles. It's just nothing. Just play the other 2 games. They ain't perfect, but better than this by a landslide.

review_text_raw:
A step-down from the last two installments. Compared to Simulacra 1 and 2, this is... pretty bad. Meh-ish. Semi-spoilers down below!
I don't mind the game's antagonist. If you've read other reviews where it says it's a ghost, the answer to that is a yes and a no. It's still a simulacra, but it takes a form of a ghost that's popular in the town's folklore and media.
That aside, the devs had made this installment rather boring and plain. You'd expect something more complex and interesting compared to the last game, but it's just... a huge down-grade from that. And I didn't even hate the second one! It was good!
BUUUT! Credit where credit's due: certain sequences are rather tense (like the entirety of Paul's house thing), and it works really well. I quite like the Atlas tracking functions, too. Ruby's actress is good, and Paul's actor is good at voice acting, so it isn't ENTIRELY bad.
Still, if you, like me, wanted to just play every installments of this franchise, just wait for the discount and get the bundle edition, since if you have the last two games, it will save you at least 30 cents if you just bought it seperately.
Overall, the experiance feels like the very first game minus the good with itty bitty of the new. Play at your own risk.
